# Libraries and the search path {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 2 &middot; PART B]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

## A library is a directory

One subdirectory per installed package
([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Managing-libraries)).

```bash
ls /usr/lib/R/library
```

You can back up a library with `tar`.

## An installed package

```bash
ls /usr/lib/R/library/grid
```

```text
DESCRIPTION  doc  help  html  INDEX  libs  Meta  NAMESPACE  R
```

| Entry | What it is |
|---|---|
| `DESCRIPTION` | Metadata, plus a `Built:` field added at install time |
| `Meta/` | Indices R uses to load the package |
| `R/` | `pkg.rdb`, `pkg.rdx`: a lazy-load database, not source files |
| `libs/` | `pkg.so`, only for packages with compiled code |
| `help/`, `html/` | Rendered documentation |

The `R/` directory holds serialized objects
([R-ints](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-ints.html#Lazy-loading)).

The installed package is not the source package.

## The `Built:` field

```bash
tail -1 /usr/lib/R/site-library/littler/DESCRIPTION
```

```text
Built: R 4.6.0; x86_64-pc-linux-gnu; 'Sun, 12 Apr 2026 10:21:37 -0500'; unix
```

`library()` uses this field. It warns about packages built under a newer R.
A package built under an older 4.x minor version loads without complaint
([library.R](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/library/base/R/library.R),
[namespace.R](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/library/base/R/namespace.R)).

Compiled packages can still break across minor versions: the R 4.6.0 upgrade
notes for Debian warn that packages such as `rlang` and `data.table` may
break until they are reinstalled
([CRAN Debian page](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/linux/debian/)). Keep one
library per R minor version.

## System, site and user libraries

| R object | Set from | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `.Library` | Fixed: `$(R RHOME)/library` | Base and recommended packages |
| `.Library.site` | `R_LIBS_SITE`, else `$(R RHOME)/site-library`; can be reassigned in `Rprofile.site` | Packages the site provides |
| *(user)* | `R_LIBS_USER`, only if the directory exists | Packages one user installed |

Only directories that exist at startup are kept
([`?.libPaths`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/libPaths.html)).

```r
.Library
.Library.site
```

```text
[1] "/usr/lib/R/library"

[1] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library" "/usr/lib/R/site-library"
```

On Debian, `/usr/lib/R/site-library` holds the `r-cran-*` packages from
`apt`, and `install.packages()` writes to `/usr/local/lib/R/site-library`
([CRAN Debian page](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/linux/debian/)).

::: {.note}
[Setting the site library]{.note-label}
R-admin recommends setting `.Library.site` in `Rprofile.site`. Setting
`R_LIBS_SITE` also works but is "not recommended"
([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Managing-libraries)).
:::

## How `.libPaths()` works

```r
.libPaths()
```

```text
[1] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library"
[2] "/usr/lib/R/site-library"
[3] "/usr/lib/R/library"
```

```r
base::.libPaths
```

```text
function (new, include.site = TRUE) 
{
    if (!missing(new)) {
        new <- Sys.glob(path.expand(new))
        paths <- c(new, if (include.site) .Library.site, .Library)
        paths <- paths[dir.exists(paths)]
        .lib.loc <<- unique(normalizePath(paths, "/"))
    }
    else .lib.loc
}
<bytecode: 0x5555558f9db0>
<environment: 0x5555558f5250>
```

1. **`.Library` is always appended.** You cannot drop the base library.
2. **Missing directories are dropped without a warning** (`dir.exists()`).
3. **Position 1 is the install target** for `install.packages()` and
   `R CMD INSTALL` (if writable).
4. **`include.site = FALSE` drops the site libraries.**

## Missing directories are dropped silently

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

`R_LIBS_USER` is set in a fresh container, but the user library is not on
the search path:

```r
Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER")
dir.exists(Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER"))
.libPaths()
```

```text
[1] "/root/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.6"

[1] FALSE

[1] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library" "/usr/lib/R/site-library"
[3] "/usr/lib/R/library"
```

The directory does not exist. Create it and it appears:

```r
dir.create(Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER"), recursive = TRUE)
.libPaths(Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER"))
.libPaths()
```

```text
[1] "/root/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.6"
[2] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library" "/usr/lib/R/site-library"
[4] "/usr/lib/R/library"
```

## Drop the user library: `.libPaths("")`

```r
.libPaths("")               # "" does not exist, so it is dropped
.libPaths()                 # site + base remain
```

```text
[1] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library" "/usr/lib/R/site-library"
[3] "/usr/lib/R/library"
```

Use it to test whether a problem goes away without the user's own packages.

::: {.note}
[Session only]{.note-label}
`.libPaths("")` changes the current session and deletes nothing. The next
R session computes the path again, and the user library is back.
:::

## Installs go to `.libPaths()[1]`

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

Start a new R session, so the user library is back on the path. `R6` has
no `Imports` and no compiled code.

```r
install.packages("R6")
```

```text
Installing package into ‘/root/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.6’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
trying URL 'https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/src/contrib/R6_2.6.1.tar.gz'
```

## Find where a package is installed

```r
list.files(.libPaths()[1])
```

```text
[1] "R6"
```

```r
list.files(file.path(.libPaths()[1], "R6"))
```

```text
[1] "DESCRIPTION" "help"  "html"  "INDEX"  "LICENSE"
[6] "Meta"  "NAMESPACE"  "NEWS.md"  "R"  "README.md"
```

From inside R: `find.package("R6")`, `packageDescription("R6")$LibPath`, and
`installed.packages(lib.loc = ...)` for one library.

## Choose the target library

```r
# 1. implicit: .libPaths()[1]
install.packages("R6")

# 2. explicit, from R
dir.create("/opt/rlibs/4.6", recursive = TRUE)
install.packages("R6", lib = "/opt/rlibs/4.6")
```

```bash
ls /opt/rlibs/4.6/
rm -Rf /opt/rlibs/4.6/R6
```

```bash
# 3. explicit, from the shell
Rscript -e 'download.packages("R6", destdir = ".")'
R CMD INSTALL --library=/opt/rlibs/4.6 R6_*.tar.gz
```

In scripts and Dockerfiles, name the library.

## Library layout for a shared server

- **Site library.** `/opt/rlibs/<R version>`. Owned by root, readable by
  everyone. The packages your organisation supports.
- **User library.** `R_LIBS_USER`, per user and R version. For exploration.
- **Project library.** `renv`, per project.

Point `.Library.site` at a path outside `$(R RHOME)`, such as `/opt/rlibs/4.6`,
so every 4.6.x installation can use it and reinstalling R does not remove it.

::: {.note}
[Recommendation]{.note-label}
Keep the site library read-only for users. Install into it from one
account or one CI job, from a recorded package list.
:::

## Library commands

| Question | Command |
|---|---|
| What is on the search path? | `.libPaths()` |
| Where will the next install go? | `.libPaths()[1]` |
| Where is this package? | `find.package("pkg")` |
| What is in this library? | `installed.packages(lib.loc = "...")[, "Version"]` |
| Is the user library the problem? | `.libPaths("")`, then retry |
| Why is my path ignored? | `dir.exists("...")` |
